TASK ID: subset-sum-to-partition

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Subset Sum to Partition. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Subset Sum and TARGET is Partition. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = SubsetSum
Subset Sum.

Instance: {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...], "target": t}
  * The numbers are non-negative integers of any size; values may repeat.
  * The target is any integer.

Yes iff some sub-list of the numbers (each position used at most once)
sums to exactly t.

Edge cases: t = 0 is always yes (the empty sub-list). t < 0 is always
no. An empty list is yes only for t = 0.

TARGET = Partition
Partition.

Instance: {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...]}
  * The numbers are non-negative integers of any size; values may repeat.

Yes iff the positions can be split into two groups whose numbers have
equal sums (every position goes in exactly one group).

Edge cases: an empty list is yes (two empty groups). An odd total is
always no. Zeros never change the answer.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-rx3a1koy

    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

Before submitting, check your reduction. problems.py has no solvers, so first write your own brute-force solvers for both problems from the definitions above. Then write tests in test_reduce.py that compare your solvers' answers on many small source instances and their reductions, run them, and revise until the tests pass. Finally write verdict.json as {"verified": true or false, "tests_run": <int>, "tests_passed": <int>}, where verified is true only if all of your tests pass. Then submit.

"command": "apply_patch <<'PATCH'
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: reduce.py
+"""Reduction from Subset Sum to Partition.
+
+The source problem (Subset Sum) instance format is:
+    {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...], "target": t}
+The target problem (Partition) instance format is:
+    {"numbers": [b1, b2, ...]}
+
+Both problems are defined in ``problems.py`` with a ``validate`` class
+method.  This module provides a single function ``reduce`` that maps a
+Subset‑Sum instance to a Partition instance preserving the answer.
+
+The classic reduction works as follows.  Let ``S`` be the sum of the
+original numbers and let ``t`` be the target.  If ``t`` is negative the
+Subset‑Sum answer is always *no*; we therefore return a Partition instance
+that is trivially *no* (an odd total).  If ``t`` is zero the answer is
+always *yes*; we return the empty list which is a yes‑instance for
+Partition.
+
+For non‑negative ``t`` we choose a target ``t'`` that satisfies ``2*t' >=
+S``.  If the original ``t`` already satisfies this inequality we keep it;
+otherwise we replace ``t`` by its complement ``S - t`` – note that the
+original instance is a yes‑instance iff a subset summing to ``S - t``
+exists (the complement of a subset summing to ``t``).  With such a ``t'``
+the value ``y = 2*t' - S`` is guaranteed to be a non‑negative integer.
+Adding ``y`` to the multiset of numbers yields a new total ``2*t'``; a
+partition into two equal halves of size ``t'`` exists exactly when the
+original Subset‑Sum instance is a yes‑instance.
+
+The construction runs in linear time and uses only integer arithmetic,
+hence it is polynomial‑time.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Dict, List
+
+from problems import SubsetSum, Partition
+
+
+def reduce(instance: Dict) -> Dict:
+    """Reduce a Subset‑Sum instance to a Partition instance.
+
+    The returned instance is a dictionary suitable for ``Partition``.
+    ``reduce`` runs in O(n) time where *n* is the number of input
+    numbers.
+    """
+    # Validate the source instance – this will raise if malformed.
+    SubsetSum.validate(instance)
+
+    numbers: List[int] = list(instance["numbers"])
+    t: int = instance["target"]
+    total = sum(numbers)
+
